title: Rapid and noninvasive artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic method for oral squamous cell carcinoma.
summary: Machine learning classified oral cancer from breath and saliva mass-spectrometry measurements in a discovery cohort and an independent validation cohort.
ai_technology: Random forest classification of breath volatile compounds
organization: Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Head and Neck Oncology; College of Stomatology; National Center for Stomatology

evidence.tested: The study reports discovery- and independent-validation-cohort diagnostic results from measured breath and saliva samples.
evidence.unknown: Validation is limited to the reported cohorts; the findings do not establish population screening or improved clinical outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: The study trained a random forest on breath-derived volatile-compound measurements to distinguish oral squamous cell carcinoma from healthy controls.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
